dedup_mechanism: Maya/strata dedups expert reads at TWO layers. (1) FETCH-level, implicit: a device-side residency table tab[layer*n_expert + expert] -> u64 VRAM pointer is read/updated inline by the route kernel (moe_route_kernel, glm_fast.cu ~3365-3569). The first token that misses an expert claims a spare slot (promotion: tab[key]=ptr), so every later token in the window/batch routing the same expert sees it resident and issues NO fetch; window-only experts that fail promote_min claim one of 8 per-layer scratch slots via a device-side bitmask (scr_used word, atomically claimed by the single route block, sticky overflow bit reuses group-owned slots). All T tokens' route->wait->fetch are enqueued back-to-back into one stream before compute, so the T*k expert copies pipeline on the PCIe link (batched DMA): moe_fetch_kernel copies one expert per iteration with 16B loads (11.5 GB/s measured); the fork's STRATA_GLM_FETCH_WIDE=1 variant uses grid(sms, k), one expert per block-group, 32B ulonglong4 loads, ~12.5 GB/s ceiling; a side-stream prefetch kernel (PF_N=8 PF_AT=fetch PF_RANK=4) copies next layer's predicted misses into next layer's spares during compute. (2) COMPUTE-level, explicit: gf::moe_win_group_kernel (glm_fast.cu:5446), a single-block/1-thread kernel that scans the window's plan_ptr[T][8] entries e=t*8+i in order and builds groups by FIRST APPEARANCE of the plan POINTER (pointer equality == same expert blob, since the residency table hands out one address per resident expert): outputs CSR arrays grp_ptr[g] (expert blob device address), grp_start[g] (offsets), grp_ent[] (entry ids e=t*8+i grouped by expert, stable order), n_groups, all on-device. O(T*k) entries (max 128: kMaxWinTokens=16, k=8), linear-search dedup, shared-memory tables. The grouped EXL3 kernels (x3::win_gu_kernel/win_down_kernel/win_combine_kernel, exl3.cu:685-746, driver win_experts():1505) then launch with grid.y = T*k (upper bound) and blocks read *n_groups from device memory and early-return past it -- no host sync, CUDA-graph-safe fixed launch geometry. Each group block reads/decodes its expert's EXL3 trellis weights ONCE (block_gemv<K,cb>(..., nc, sm)) and applies them to up to kTok=8 member activations at once (activations staged in shared xb[2*kTok*kCols], mma.m16n8k16 with activations as the 8 B-columns on sm80+); excess members in kTok-sized passes; gate/up completion via per-group atomic counters (pair_last). Down-projections write PER-ENTRY partials part[e][n_embd] (not per-group), so win_combine_kernel (grid (n_embd/128, T)) gathers each token's k entries in plan order, weights by plan_w, adds the CPU-lane part (cpu_flag/cpu_part) and shared expert -- bit-exact per token vs the single-token path. Ordering in the window driver (glm_window.cu:579-767, STRATA_GLM_WIN_BATCH default ON, STRATA_GLM_WIN_X3 default ON): all T routes+fetches enqueued -> shared-expert mv (ncol=T) -> moe_win_group -> x3::win_experts -> per-token moe_cpu_wait (host AVX2 lane answers consumed after GPU compute, hidden under it). Measured effect: ~19 distinct experts of ~24 routed per window layer (~80% dedup); window cost model in verify.hpp: union of misses = 1.75x/2.4x/3.05x one token's at T=2/3/4. Instrumentation: 'glm window union CUDA%d: distinct/routed' stat via host sort+unique over routed ids (glm_window.cu:1141-1151,1729). NOT implemented (documented gap in EXL3-50Tps-RESEARCH.md): AcceptMoE-style commitment weighting and residency-aware pruning of the union -- ranked R1 for the 50 t/s push; SpecMoE-style larger windows ranked R2. The '70 t/s multi-draft/SpecFit/batch DMA' phrasing in the task context matches this planned work, not shipped code.

transferable_design: Portable design for a vLLM EXL3 MoE kernel on offload-bound rigs: (1) PLAN REPRESENTATION -- keep per-(token,slot) parallel arrays plan_ptr (u64 device address of the expert blob, 0 = absent/CPU), plan_w (router weight), plan_id, shaped [T][8]. The device pointer is simultaneously the dedup key and the kernel's weight index: no id->row table walk in the hot kernel. (2) WHERE THE UNION IS COMPUTED -- on the GPU, not the host: after all T window/batch tokens' routers finish (their routes+fetches enqueued back-to-back so DMA pipelines), run one tiny single-block kernel (1 active thread is fine at T*k<=128) that scans entries e=t*8+i in order, linear-searches a first-appearance list of plan_ptr values, and emits a CSR: grp_ptr[g], grp_start[g], grp_ent[] (entry ids in stable order), n_groups, all in device memory. (3) LAUNCH GEOMETRY -- launch the grouped GEMV with grid.y = T*k (upper bound) and have each block early-return when blockIdx.y >= *n_groups read from device memory: fixed launch shape, no D2H sync, CUDA-graph capturable. (4) KERNEL BODY -- one block per (row-chunk of n_ff, group): load/dequant the expert's weights ONCE into registers/shared, then loop the group's members in passes of up to 8 activations (staged in shared memory; on sm80+ feed them as the 8 n-columns of mma.m16n8k16, exllamav3-style); gate+up blocks coordinate the fused swiglu through per-group atomic counters (last-arriver applies activation fn). (5) INDEXING STAGED ROWS -- write DOWN-projection results as PER-ENTRY partials part[e][n_embd] where e=t*8+i (NOT per-group), so a final per-token combine kernel (grid (n_embd/128, T)) reassembles each token's k experts in plan order, scales by plan_w, and adds CPU-lane and shared-expert contributions -- numerically bit-identical to the single-token path, which matters for greedy spec-decode acceptance. (6) DMA GROUPING -- cross-token fetch dedup comes free from a device-side residency table (layer,expert)->pointer updated inline at route time: the first miss claims a free VRAM slot (promotion) and later tokens see it resident; transient window experts land in per-layer scratch slots allocated by a device-side bitmask (no atomics needed if the router is one block). The copy kernel should be one expert per block-group with 32-byte vector loads (measured 11.5-12.5 GB/s on gen4 x16 vs cudaMemcpy's 10.7), and a low-SM side stream prefetches the next layer's top-rank predicted misses into that layer's spares during compute. (7) OVERLAP -- publish CPU-lane expert requests through a host-mapped ring with sequence numbers before the grouped GPU launch; consume answers with a spin-wait kernel after it, so host GEMV hides under grouped compute. (8) EXPECTED WIN -- measured union multipliers 1.75x/2.4x/3.05x single-token misses at T=2/3/4 (~80% distinct/routed per layer at T=3); the unimplemented next step (AcceptMoE commitment-weighted pruning + bigger windows) is projected 520->~300 MB/token on this rig.
